title: Robert Reade (Paris) to his cousin, 19 April 1641 (BL Harley MS 7001 ff. 148-149; DECODE R7766)

steps.what: Fetched R7766 record and 4 full-resolution images with the session cookie.
Read signature 'R. Reade' and endorsement 'my Cousin Reade from Paris'; identified the writer as Robert Reade of the Windebank household in exile.
Transcribed the two cipher passages (254 groups, numbers 2-729 plus symbol letters).
Tried DECODE key R8694 (Mr Browne, Add MS 72438): codes stop at 371, alphabet gives no sense.
Searched DECODE metadata for Windebank; found R9115 (Add MS 32256 f. 4, Windebank to his son, Paris 1640-42), a Deciphering Branch reconstruction; read both pages of it.
Applied the key: 'in case a proclamation shall goe out against ... they have not enough against him to confiscate his fortune ... refusall to return ...'.
Re-read doubtful glyphs at full resolution against the key's symbol list: 8=phi (s), D=n-sign, 2=reversed c (d), delta (t).
Web search for the letter and a Reade/Windebank decipherment in print.
Filled code groups blank in the reconstruction by alphabetical slot and context (524 return, 562 secure, 573 they, 660 willing; 15 weaker conjectures).
Re-read the key sheet side notes: 203 done, 729 ct. (Court); two conjectures become key readings; 94.0% read.
Ranked bracket-consistent candidates for the 13 blank groups with the en-1640s LM in context (lmfill.py): scores favour short words and do not separate the candidates; no value upgraded.
Calendar of the Clarendon State Papers vol. 1 (1872) full text: Windebank papers end at his flight; no Reade letter or 1641 key.

Constrained search (beamfill.py): all corpus words in each blank's alphabetical bracket scored in context by the en-1640s LM; brackets empty for 5 open code values (key order not monotone), top candidates elsewhere are function words or noise; nothing upgraded.

Seeded coordinate-ascent anneal (annealfill.py) over the blank code groups, 2000-word vocabulary, LM objective on the full passages: converges to function words (was, he, and, that); no sense reading, nothing upgraded.

CSP Domestic 1640-41 full text: Reade's Paris letters to Thomas Windebank (SP 16) calendared with cipher sentences unread; confirms recipient; the originals (same code) are the only further source, not online.

Correction after an outside check of the write-up against the key images: R9115's continuation page plainly reads '562 strong', which a later line of key.py had overwritten with a rebuilt 'secure'; the key value is restored ('how his person can be strong', i.e. safe; H). 660 'willing' regraded from rebuilt to conjecture: on the key's first page 660 is blank among the y-words (652 you, 662 you, 664 your, 666 yet), a w-word would stand near 636 will, and no y-word gives the sense. The partly legible key entry '573. u. th...' (end under a ruled line) fits the rebuilt they/the but does not confirm it. Re-measured: 193 key, 8 rebuilt (573 occurs three times, not four), 14 conjectured of 215; 93.5% (was 94.0%).

Push-to-95% pass: the margin entry for 650 beside 591-600 on R9115 f.1 examined at full resolution (crop rotated): it reads '650. w[r]it' with an h written above (writ? with? wait?), not 'way'. No reading fits 'The only ___ is conceived to be that His Majesty will please to prevent'; 650 stays conjecture. The other 12 open code values were checked for side notes in the 300-700 margin lists of both key pages: none present. 201 of 215 (93.5%) stays; 95% needs 205, i.e. 4 more of the 14 single-occurrence blanks, which have no key material.

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The Deciphering Branch reconstruction of the Windebank family cipher on DECODE R9115 (BL Add MS 32256, headed 'Windebank to his Son ... 1642'), filed in another volume and not tied to this letter, was found to read it; 5 values (8 groups) were rebuilt here.

gaps.detail: blank in the only surviving key reconstruction (R9115); conjectured from context and alphabetical slot

outcome.notes: 193/215 significant tokens from key values, 8 from values rebuilt here, 14 conjectured (re-measured 30 Sept 2026 with key.py).

prior.where: Not printed or calendared; the key reconstruction exists (R9115) but no decipherment of this letter

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up the coding agent with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
